description:
Advances: specled.prime, specled.next, specled.package

From the pre-ship critical review (consolidated 2026-07-25, CF1 + U9). Tier-1: the taught protocol sentence is FALSE as shipped and is replicated into adopter repos by the bootstrap skill.

VERIFIED BY EXECUTION (consolidator): `mix spec.check --base definitely-not-a-real-ref --no-run-commands 2>&1 | tail -2` puts `** (Mix) --base ... does not resolve to a commit` AFTER the verdict line. Since a failing run always raises, and a terminal interleaves both streams, "The last line is the verdict" is false on every failure path in ordinary use, not just under 2>&1.

Current sentence (25 occurrences, must stay byte-identical everywhere):
"The last line is the verdict — `spec.check result=…`; nothing above it, including `validate status=…`, is the verdict."

Required properties of the replacement:
1. TRUE under merged stdout+stderr and in a terminal.
2. Anchors on the PREFIX (`spec.check result=`), not on line position.
3. Defines the absence case: no verdict line present => treat as failure (non-zero exit is the forgery-proof signal; exit codes verified non-zero on every failure path).
4. Still distinguishes the verdict from `validate status=…` (the original bug this epic exists to fix).
5. Byte-identical on every surface.

Proposed wording (refine if you can do better while keeping 1-5):
"The verdict is the last stdout line starting with `spec.check result=` — not `validate status=…`. A non-zero exit means failure even if no verdict line appears."

Surfaces to update (all 25 occurrences): lib/specled_ex/prime.ex, lib/specled_ex/next.ex, test/mix/tasks/spec_prime_task_test.exs, test/mix/tasks/spec_next_task_test.exs, .spec/specs/prime.spec.md, .spec/specs/next.spec.md, .spec/AGENTS.md, .claude/rules/specled.md, docs/adoption.md (x3), docs/concepts.md, docs/coverage.md, skills/spec-led-bootstrap/SKILL.md (x3), references/adoption-phases.md (x3), references/detection-matrix.md, references/configurable-levers.md (x2).

ALSO (U9, same files): docs/coverage.md:47 appends the sentence to a paragraph about `mix spec.cover.test` exit codes, but spec.cover.test never emits a verdict line (print_verdict exists only in spec.check.ex/spec.validate.ex) — relocate it to a real spec.check passage in that file or drop that occurrence. Same for the mid-list occurrence in configurable-levers.md if it lands on an unrelated passage.

Also consider hoisting the sentence to ONE shared constant in lib/ referenced by prime.ex, next.ex and both test files (CF3) — it contains U+2014 and U+2026, so retyped copies can differ invisibly.

OUT OF SCOPE: the tier=usage grammar change, tagged_tests attribution fixes, drain-helper channel work, fixture severity mix (all batched to the fast-follow). No lib/ behavior change beyond the sentence constant.

NOTE (out-of-repo handoff): .claude/rules/specled.md is agent-rules-sync-managed. The in-repo edit is correct, but the vault source at ~/dev/mz/agentic-dotfiles/llms/workflows/agent-rules/rules/specled.md needs the identical reword or the next sync reverts it. Record this in the completion record; the orchestrator applies it.

Verification: mix compile --warnings-as-errors && mix test && mix format --check-formatted && mix deps.unlock --check-unused && mix spec.check (bare). Plus: prove by execution that the new sentence is true on a failure path (run spec.check with a bad --base under 2>&1 and confirm the sentence text accurately describes what a reader sees).

Reasoning: Both of the newest VERIFY's gaps reproduce on cold structural read, and the one I was asked to stress — Gap 2's command-output echo — is genuine default-on production wiring, not a fixture artifact. Trace: verifier.ex:637 builds the finding message as "exit_code=<N>\n" <> the subprocess's verbatim stdout (command_failure_details/3, :627-649), verifier.ex:614-623 wraps it into the verification_command_failed finding, and both spec.check.ex:234 (print_validation_findings/2) and spec.validate.ex:114 render that finding with a SINGLE Mix.shell().info("[#{severity}] ... :: #{message}") — so every captured line after the first lands at column 0 on the task's own stdout, above the verdict; spec.check.ex:166-171 run_commands?/1 returns true unless --no-run-commands, so a downstream repo's plain `mix spec.check` executes every `execute: true` kind: command verification by default. The verifier's fixture supplied only the CONTENT of the echoed line; the emission path is real, and the "only stdout line that starts with the task name" clause of specled.tasks.verdict_line (mix_tasks.spec.md:270-279) is therefore false and asserted exactly once anywhere — spec_tasks_test.exs:183, on the spec.validate --output path, with no spec.check equivalent. Gap 1 is the stronger of the two and is not wording pedantry: branch_check.ex:637-651 validate_base!/2 raises a plain ArgumentError from inside SpecLedEx.branch_check at spec.check.ex:124-129, i.e. AFTER the `validate status=...` line is printed at spec.check.ex:110-112 and with no verdict, so `mix spec.check --base origin/main` against an unfetched ref leaves `validate status=pass errors=0 warnings=0` as the literal last stdout line — the exact line the read protocol shipped in prime.ex:82 and next.ex:318 tells agents is NOT the verdict. index.ex:89-95 detect_spec_dir/1 (RuntimeError, reached from spec.check.ex:78 / spec.validate.ex:53) is the same class. No test covers either.

Mechanical counts re-checked independently and correct: `git diff --name-only 14f6e72..HEAD` = 15 files; all 15 fall inside the amended Allowed list (4 lib, 4 test incl. the audit-authorized spec_check_test.exs, 3 subject specs, 4 audit-authorized attestation specs); 0 match any Out-of-Scope glob (no CHANGELOG.md, VERSION, docs/**, README.md, skills/**, .spec/AGENTS.md, .claude/rules/**, package.spec.md, coverage/**, review/**, case.ex, decisions/**). I read all four attestation diffs — each adds only a "Branch reconciliation note" paragraph above the spec-verification fence with no requirement or claim-wording change. Intent-level Out of Scope holds: every Mix.raise retained with the verdict immediately before it, print_verdict duplicated as a private helper in both task modules with no new lib/ file, the sort result only ever piped into Enum.each with record_evidence/3 (spec.check.ex:139) receiving the unsorted report, rename-in-place with no bare `status=` survivor, mix.exs/mix.lock absent. The new spec.check.ex:70 guard `rest != [] or invalid != []` is exactly SpecLedEx.TaskArgs.validate!/3's raise condition (task_args.ex:9-16), so no spurious verdict can precede a continuing run. Attempt 1's Gaps 1 and 3 and its scope violation are genuinely closed — `state wrote` replaces the task-name-prefixed --output notice, and the new mixed-severity fixture at spec_tasks_test.exs:610-681 makes BOTH validation-side sort call sites falsifiable (warning_index < error_index asserted for spec.validate at :659 and spec.check at :678).

Two corrections to the verifier's Gap 2 framing, neither changing the routing (the FAIL and both gaps stand): (1) ".spec/specs/spec_system.spec.md:74-76 ... puts real `spec.validate result=...` lines onto spec.check's stdout today" is wrong twice — those two kind: command entries carry no `execute:` key and verifier.ex:377 gates execution on bool_field(verification, "execute"), so they do not run; and `spec.validate`-prefixed output would not forge `spec.check`'s own anchor on a spec.check run anyway. The reachable case requires the OUTER task's own name at column 0 in captured output, which nothing prevents but which no shipped config produces today. (2) "a reader taking the first match on the anchor the ticket teaches gets the inverted answer" overstates the harm: the protocol sentence actually shipped (prime.ex:82, next.ex:318) teaches a LAST-LINE anchor, not a prefix grep, and the echoed line sits above the verdict, so the taught protocol still returns the right answer on that path. The clause is still literally false and untested — that is what the gap rests on, and it survives both corrections.

Authority: both fixes are inside this ticket, no human escalation needed on authority grounds. .spec/specs/mix_tasks.spec.md is in Allowed and the specled rule permits requirement rewording with spec + code + verification in one PR. Gap 2 specifically does NOT require re-opening the read protocol — because prime/next teach last-line, not prefix-grep, and last-line stays true on the command-echo path, narrowing the "only stdout line" clause is a self-contained spec edit plus tests.

Bounce reason: Two items; take the decidable resolution below rather than re-litigating the design, because this is the second of the ticket's bounce budget. (a) Gap 1 — do BOTH halves, don't pick one. Scope the specled.tasks.verdict_line statement to paths where the task itself reports a verdict (raises that fire before the task has emitted any output, i.e. index.ex:89-95 detect_spec_dir/1 and the File.Error from SpecLedEx.write_state at spec.validate.ex:81, are legitimately out of scope — there is no misleading last line to misread), AND fix the --base path in code, because it is the one path that leaves `validate status=...` as the last stdout line and so actively defeats the protocol prime.ex:82 / next.ex:318 now ship. Simplest code fix: validate --base up front in spec.check.ex alongside validate_min_strength!/1 (spec.check.ex:294) and print the fail verdict before raising, mirroring what you already did there; add a test that drains the shell on that path. Update the specled.tasks.verdict_line.stdout_contract scenario (mix_tasks.spec.md:295-304) to match whatever scoping you land on. (b) Gap 2 — narrow the "only stdout line that starts with the task name" clause to lines the task itself emits (e.g. "the only line the task itself emits matching `^<task> result=`"), stating explicitly that verbatim-relayed `kind: command` output is exempt, and back it with tests: add the spec.check-side counterpart to spec_tasks_test.exs:183 (which today exists only for spec.validate), and add one test proving that a failing kind: command verification whose captured output contains a task-name-prefixed line still leaves the verdict as the last message. Do not change the prime/next protocol sentence — its last-line anchor is what survives, and it must keep holding after (a).
